## Meeting Room Booking System v1.0.0 — delivered

All three subtasks are accepted: dev's implementation (subtask-1, reviewed with source-level evidence), QA's independent verification (subtask-2), and the release README (subtask-3).

### What you get (5 files, shared copies in inbox/dev/ plus README.md)
| File | Size | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `booking.py` | 14,708 B | Core logic + JSON store (stdlib only) |
| `server.py` | 9,726 B | `ThreadingHTTPServer` web server + JSON API, serves the page |
| `index.html` | 24,373 B | Single self-contained UI (inline CSS/JS, no CDN, works offline) |
| `selftest.py` | 7,152 B | Plain-assert self-test |
| `README.md` | 3,463 B | User guide / release notes |

### How to use it (2 steps)
1. Put all four code files in **one** folder, then run:
   ```
   python3 server.py
   ```
   (optional: `--port 8080 --data bookings.json --rooms rooms.json`)
2. Open `http://localhost:8080`, or the LAN URL printed at startup (e.g. `http://192.168.1.20:8080`) so colleagues share **one** calendar. Data lives in a single `bookings.json` next to the server — copy that file to back it up.

Day to day: pick a date (defaults to today) and optionally a room → read the per-room 07:00–20:00 timeline to see free gaps at a glance → book room/date/start/end (15-min steps)/title/organizer → a clashing slot is refused with a message naming the clashing booking, while back-to-back meetings are allowed → cancel with confirm + optional reason: the slot frees instantly and the record stays as a greyed-out, struck-through entry behind the "show cancelled" toggle.

### How double bookings are actually prevented
Every create runs inside one `threading.Lock` critical section: read all bookings from disk → validate → scan same-room/same-date **active** bookings for overlap using half-open intervals (`start < other.end and end > other.start`, so 10:00–11:00 and 11:00–12:00 coexist) → append → atomic `tempfile` + `os.replace` write. human_interventions.text: I am 25 years old, have HKD 1,000,000, and would like to invest in US stocks. Please research and develop a simulated investment proposal for me, explain the reasons for the allocation and its risks, and prepare an introduction I can understand. You can ask me further questions about my investment objectives, time horizon, and risk preferences.

Thanks — before I build the simulated proposal, five quick questions (short answers are fine; if you'd rather not decide, I'll use the defaults in brackets):

1) **Goal & time horizon** — what is this HKD 1,000,000 for, and when might you need the money? [default: long-term wealth growth, 10+ years, no withdrawal needed]
2) **Risk tolerance** — if the portfolio temporarily fell, what's the largest drop you could sit through without selling in panic: ~15%, ~30%, or ~50%? [default: ~30%]
3) **Income vs growth** — do you need regular dividend/income payouts, or should everything be reinvested for growth? [default: growth, dividends reinvested]
4) **Practical set-up** — do you already have an emergency cash buffer (3–6 months of expenses) and any other investments/debt? Are you comfortable with USD exposure and holding US-domiciled ETFs/stocks (e.g., US estate-tax paperwork over USD 60k for non-US persons)? [default: yes buffer exists, no other assets, USD acceptable]
5) **Preferences/restrictions** — happy with mostly broad index ETFs plus a small satellite of individual stocks, or do you want individual stocks only? Any sectors or companies you want excluded? [default: core ETFs + small stock satellite, no exclusions]

I'll also ask my research and risk teammates to work in parallel, so even a one-line reply per question keeps us on schedule.

1) GOAL AND HORIZON: long-term wealth building, roughly a 5 to 10 year horizon. I have no planned withdrawal inside that window. 2) RISK TOLERANCE: moderate - I could sit through about a 25 to 30 percent temporary drop without selling, but not 50 percent. 3) INCOME VS GROWTH: growth, reinvest dividends. I do not need payouts. 4) PRACTICAL SET-UP: yes, I already hold about six months of living expenses in cash separately, and this HKD 1,000,000 is money I can leave invested. No other investments and no debt. I am comfortable with USD exposure, and thank you for flagging the US estate-tax point for non-US persons above USD 60,000 - please note it explicitly in the proposal and mention the UCITS alternative, then make a clear recommendation rather than leaving it open. 5) PREFERENCES: core broad index ETFs plus a small satellite of individual stocks is exactly what I want. No sector or company exclusions. Please make clear which figures are historical and dated versus which are assumptions, and remember this is a simulation, not advice or a real trade.
